The quotation explicitly states "To him I shall come when I go beyond this life," indicating a belief in existence after death. This directly supports option (B).  

Option (A) is incorrect because the passage emphasizes faith and internal spiritual realization ("he who has faith and doubts not"), not rituals.  
Option (C) is not supported; the text focuses on faith and union with Brahman, not a list of right actions or speech to please gods.  
Option (D) is incorrect because the passage describes a single divine reality ("Brahman") that "enfolds the whole universe," reflecting monism or monotheistic tendencies in the Upanishads, not polytheism.  

Final answer: (B)
